gradients.name: window-bar
gradients.purpose: The --window-bar custom property: every window's bar, the overlay's, the search view's, the Grind Tracker's, the Personal Bests window's and the Item Card's, and setup's and the site's.

gradients.name: game-button
gradients.purpose: The game's bright blue window buttons: the overlay's toolbar, the search view's back button, and the × and buttons on every overlay window's bar.

gradients.name: game-button-hover
gradients.purpose: A game-blue button under the pointer.

gradients.name: button-hover
gradients.purpose: Setup's primary button under the pointer, and held.

gradients.name: button-light
gradients.purpose: Setup's secondary buttons, the overlay's light icon and text buttons, and the site's tabs and secondary buttons.

gradients.name: button-light-hover
gradients.purpose: A light-steel button under the pointer.

gradients.name: exp-fill
gradients.purpose: The game's EXP gauge lime: the Grind Tracker's EXP gauge fill and the Personal Bests window's lanes, and nothing else.

gradients.name: exp-track
gradients.purpose: The light grey track under the Grind Tracker's EXP gauge's fill; the Personal Bests window's lanes have none.

headline.purpose: The Map Name in Title Lettering on the title panel and setup's recognised test read; Time to Level and setup's step headings at the same size in plain ink. Held, the Time to Level figure and the rates drop to Light, never a fainter colour (the Best row's figure doesn't move, and stays bold); with no figure to give, the slot says why in 13px Light Panel Ink Steel, never a bare dash.

street.purpose: Above the Map Name in the same Title Lettering, the Mini Map's own idiom.

section-heading.purpose: Map, Navigation and Mobs, and the Hunting Target's mob under Navigation, in Panel Ink: one step above the 13px bold rows they head.

status.purpose: The no-map status in the Map Name's slot, plain Panel Ink with no outline, so it doesn't read as a map name.

window-name.purpose: The window's name and the search view's title on the grey window bar; setup's step count.

title.purpose: Portal destinations, summary and rate values, the Hunting Target's figures and "You're here".

body-reading.purpose: Setup's prose and the search field: read at rest, one step larger than the overlay.

body.purpose: Overlay notes, the mob and rates tables, the suggestions; tabular figures.

body-small.purpose: Positions, labels, units, headers, the route, the arrival's trip, candidate rows and key hints.

label.purpose: Tags and the "Not sure" chip (uppercase only there).

site-title.purpose: Each site page's one h1: the hero's title on the home page, the FAQ's at its top; balanced; 32px/38px on phones.

site-opener.purpose: Heading each feature and section of the home page, led by a legend mark where it has one; 26px/32px on phones.

site-topic.purpose: Heading each FAQ group, held beside its questions as they go by, led by a legend mark where it has one; 20px/26px on phones.

site-subhead.purpose: The subheads within a large FAQ group (The panel, Mobs, Bug Reports).

site-lede.purpose: The hero's sentence, a feature's words and the owl's; 16px/26px on phones.

site-body.purpose: The site's prose; 15px/24px under 640px. The site's own reading scale, outside the overlay's ramp on purpose: read at rest in a window up to 1200px wide.

site-answer.purpose: A question's answer, and the line under a FAQ group's heading (in Ink Steel).

site-question.purpose: A question, folded to its one line beside the panel's fold button, as the panel folds a section to its heading.

shadows.name: window-inner-ring
shadows.purpose: Just inside every window's frame: the panel's, the Grind Tracker's, the Personal Bests window's, the Item Card's, setup's and the site's; 0.65 on the title-marking hint.

shadows.name: bar-top-highlight
shadows.purpose: The top edge of setup's window bar; 0.6 on the doubt chip, 0.3 on setup's primary button, solid #fff on light steel.

shadows.name: game-button-bevel
shadows.purpose: The game's blue buttons; their white icon carries drop-shadow(0 1px 0 rgba(0, 50, 90, 0.45)).

shadows.name: pressed-steel
shadows.purpose: A held deep-steel button (--pressed-steel); on the site, a held Download.

shadows.name: pressed-light-steel
shadows.purpose: A held light-steel button (--pressed-light-steel); on the site, a held tab or secondary button.

shadows.name: glyph-ring
shadows.purpose: The dark edge on mob dots, the you dot and the orange dots; the alert dot adds 0 0 0 2px #fff.

shadows.name: title-lettering
shadows.purpose: The --title-lettering text-shadow: a map's title only.

shadows.name: light-edge
shadows.purpose: A text-shadow on every line of text on the panel's body, so a busy scene can't swallow it.

shadows.name: pressed-epic
shadows.purpose: A held great-deal badge, on Epic Purple.

shadows.name: pressed-unique
shadows.purpose: A held steal badge, on Unique Gold.

tints.name: row-hover
tints.purpose: Edit Blue at 8% (--row-hover): suggestion and result rows, the Personal Bests window's rows and the site's questions under the pointer.

motion.name: ease-out-expo
motion.purpose: The one ease for motion that answers the pointer, in CSS; where script drives it, 1 − 2^(−10t), scaled to land exactly. Never anything that overshoots.

motion.name: answer-duration
motion.purpose: How long a motion that answers the player may run: a card opening out of what it describes, a zoom, a fold, from a first frame already readable.

motion.name: mark-card-dive
motion.purpose: The Mark Card's close-up diving from the map at the preview's scale to the spot, interpolated in log scale; the windows' one authored motion so far.

motion.name: game-change
motion.value: 0ms, or a cross-fade of 150ms at most
motion.purpose: What the game changes (a new map, an EXP reading, a note, the arrival, the Pace Trace, the lanes) changes at once: never a slide, a count-up or a bounce.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Everything at once, in its final state: the close-up opens on the spot, the site minimap's dot steps from portal to portal, the hero is its still shot.

breakpoints.name: panel-narrow
breakpoints.purpose: The panel at a raised text scale: the summary's figures stack, mob rows become labelled cards.

breakpoints.name: bests-fold-lanes
breakpoints.purpose: The Personal Bests window: each lane goes under its figure.

breakpoints.name: bests-narrow
breakpoints.purpose: The Personal Bests window: the date may wrap and the share's header says "% of solo".

breakpoints.name: bests-cards
breakpoints.purpose: The Personal Bests window: each map becomes a card, its lane the card's width.

breakpoints.name: site-minimap
breakpoints.purpose: The site: three columns, the Mini Map docked in the left one.

breakpoints.name: site-get-started
breakpoints.purpose: The site: Get started's game window goes under its steps.

breakpoints.name: site-one-column
breakpoints.purpose: The site: every row and group is one column at the measure.

breakpoints.name: site-phone
breakpoints.purpose: The site: the window meets the page's edges, the tab strip alone sticks, the hero's buttons run the full width.

components.description: A button in a window's body rather than its bar: light steel with a near-black icon. components.name: Mark Card
components.description: The card of the ring or spawn point's dot the pointer is on, or of the Hidden Portal row: a close-up of the spot (OSMS's picture around the portal or spawn point at half the game's size, 104px tall, diving to it from the map in 360ms on an exponential ease-out, at once with reduced motion), then the destination, its street and a tag per kind, or the mob, its level and its spawn points. components.name: Grind Tracker Figures
components.description: The Session's figures set into the Grind Tracker's body on near-opaque Window Lavender: Time to Level with the light reset button at the far end, the rates as the panel's summary in miniature, the Pace Trace under them, then the share and deaths lines. The rates are Last 5 min, Session once it runs longer, and on a map with a Personal Best from its history the Best row, its "Best" a plain link that opens the Personal Bests window (Portal Blue and underlined under the pointer) and its light × removing that best from the history. While Last 5 min beats the best over a full 5 minutes on the map, an 11px You Yellow star follows its period; its room is kept while it's off. The Pace Trace races the last 5 minutes against the 5 before them as split times against a ghost: the earlier pace a flat Ink Slate line, the trace in Panel Ink stepping up at each gain, the gap shaded at 8%, the player's 8px dot and the split by it; once the best's pace is within reach it joins in you-edge gold ending in a best's star, the lead over it lit in You Yellow. It moves only as the EXP does. Held (warming up, paused, or the EXP bar unread), the figures drop to Light, never fainter, all but the Best row's.

components.name: Site
components.description: The Minerva site at owlofminerva.app has three main tabs: Home, Map Leaderboards and FAQ. The home page shows what Minerva does a feature at a time; the FAQ holds the details as the questions players ask. Each is one of the game's windows opened wide in the browser (up to 1200px, 28px down) on Quest Helper Glass over white, in setup's opaque language and the site's own reading scale (16px/26px body). Its sticky head is setup's window bar (32px owl, name, version, steel Download) over the tab band (the lavender mixed 12% toward Frame Navy) holding one raised Light Steel tab per page; the page you're on is the open tab, 4px taller and joined to the lavender (aria-current="page"). A feature row is its shot on a 440px stage and its words: a Site Opener heading led by the panel's legend mark, a sentence or two, then its most-asked questions. Each question is a native details row in an inset box, folded to its question with the panel's 19px fold button at its right; a question is written once, on the FAQ. The owl speaks twice, as the game's NPCs do; the hero films how Minerva reads a map, moved only by the scroll; from 1440px a Mini Map docks beside the window.

Every portal, even the hidden ones

The panel shows the map you're on with every portal ringed, and lists its Hidden Portals, the ones the game doesn't show.

What's a Hidden Portal?

A portal the game doesn't mark on the map, so you only find it by walking over it.

Why does the panel say "Not sure"?

Minerva read the minimap's title but can't be certain which map it is.

narrative.northStar: The Window the Game Forgot to Ship
narrative.overview:
The overlay is one more of the game's windows laid over the screen, built from the two it sits beside. From the Mini Map it takes the light grey window bar with the window's name and small bright blue buttons, and the sky-blue title panel with the map's Map Mark beside the Street Name over the Map Name in light lettering outlined in blue. From the Quest Helper it takes the see-through periwinkle body with near-black text. The minimap's legend supplies the glyphs: blue portal rings, red mob dots, and the player's yellow dot. The pixel-art owl, the app icon, is the window's mark. The game supplies the materials and one signature move; organisation, hierarchy and density come from a working tool: EXP pace first when it is tracked, then the map and its hidden exits, then the way to the Hunting Target, then the mobs, then the credit. It is not a screenshot of a game window.

It is light because the game's windows are light, see-through because the game's windows over the screen are, and dense because it is read in glances between attacks. Every state is drawn in the same window. Doubt and problems get the game's orange, and nothing else does. The confirmed rejection is the generic dark dev-tools card with a stats table on top, which this world replaced. Setup is a window on the desktop rather than over the game: it keeps an opaque lavender body, navy ink and steel buttons under the same grey window bar, and shows a recognised map exactly as the overlay's title panel will. The project's site is that same opaque window opened wide in the browser: a home page that shows what Minerva does a feature at a time, the Map Leaderboards, where players' Personal Bests stand side by side map by map, and a FAQ that answers everything else, its raised tabs its pages.

Every window takes the pointer. The overlay is always clickable, but a click never takes the keyboard from the game except in the search view, where the query field needs it. The Settings window takes it as it opens, and again on a Change, where a hotkey's new keys are pressed, or on the Deal Margin field; a click back in the game gives it back, and the window stays open. The panel is dragged by its window bar or title panel when it sits inside the game or is detached, and resized by its sides or bottom corners, width only. Its buttons and setup's buttons carry the game's hover, pressed and keyboard-focus states; list rows in the search view take a faint hover tint. Its height follows its content. Motion answers the player (see Motion): the Mark Card's close-up dives from the map to a portal's or spawn point's spot as the pointer comes to rest on it, while what the game changes, a new map or an EXP reading (and with it the Grind Tracker's Pace Trace and forecast), changes at once, as the game's own windows do. On the site two things move with the scroll, as the game's minimap dot moves only as the character walks: the site minimap's yellow dot and the site hero's film. One moves with a click: a map's Map Leaderboard switching Level Band, its Characters in both bands sliding to their new rank and the lanes regrowing. With reduced motion nothing moves: the close-up opens on the spot, the dot steps from portal to portal, the hero is its still shot and the band switches at once.
keyCharacteristics: The Mini Map's light grey window bar and sky-blue title panel over the Quest Helper's see-through periwinkle body, in a 4px-cornered frame.
The Map Mark beside Street Name over Map Name in light lettering outlined in blue, as the Mini Map draws its title; the same mark at half size beside a map's name wherever else it shows.

Three icon vocabularies only: minimap glyphs (portal ring, mob dot, you dot and the you yellow star) and the Map Preview's rings, route rings and teleport arrows in CSS and SVG, drawn line icons on the game's small blue buttons, and the pixel-art owl as the window's mark. The Map Marks are the game's own art, not a vocabulary of ours.
Near-black ink with a faint light edge on the see-through body; navy ink on setup's opaque lavender.
Game orange appears only for doubt and problems.
NEXON's Maplestory typeface throughout, Light and Bold; numeric columns right-aligned.

Buttons in every window have the game's hover, pressed and focus states. Motion answers the player, in one exponential ease-out, and never runs on a timer: in the panel, the Mark Card's close-up diving to the spot; on the site, the minimap's dot and the hero's film, both moved by the scroll, and a Map Leaderboard's band switch, moved by the click. With reduced motion nothing moves.

rules.name: The Orange Means Doubt Rule
rules.body: Game orange marks only uncertainty and problems: the "Not sure" chip, problem notes, the collapsed alert dot. A confirmed state never uses it, so orange can't become decoration. Search tiers are told apart by weight and ink, never by orange.

rules.name: The Minimap Legend Rule
rules.body: Portal blue, mob red and you yellow come from the minimap's legend and keep that meaning. Blue is for portals, red is for mobs (the mob rows' dots, and the Map Preview's dot on every Spawn Point, as the minimap dots mobs) and yellow is for where the player is, with no other uses but one: you yellow also draws a best (the star for the Grind Tracker's new best, the Personal Bests window's best of all maps and, on the site's Map Leaderboards, the entry a link from the Personal Bests window names, and on the Pace Trace, the Best's pace in you-edge gold ending in a best's star, the lead lit over it and the split against it), since all are about the player. The Map Preview adds two ring colours from OSMS Data Explorer, each with one meaning: Teleport Green for a portal within the map and its arrow, Unknown Grey for a portal to a map not in the data. Blue stays the ring of a portal to another map, Doors included; green is never a tag. Route Magenta is the panel's own and means one thing, the way to the Hunting Target or the Destination: the wide ring around a portal the route takes next, the Navigation section's mark, and the ring at a Destination's route's end.

rules.name: The EXP Lime Rule
rules.body: The lime of the game's EXP gauge draws EXP and nothing else: the EXP bar's reading in the Grind Tracker, a map's best EXP/h on its lane in the Personal Bests window (each Visit's on its own), and each entry's EXP/h on its lane on the site's Map Leaderboards. Not progress in general, not a rank, and never a highlight: the linked Character's lane is lime like everyone's, and You Yellow's star marks it. The ground a death took back, the forecast's notches, a lane's notches for its other Visits and a ruler's notches are the gauge's frame grey, never lime: they aren't the reading.

rules.name: The Item Grade Rule
rules.body: A deal is graded as the game grades its items, blue, then purple, then gold, which players already read as good, better, best: a good deal is the deep steel button, a great one (20% or more below the Deal Line) Epic Purple (`#8456d1` to `#6435b0`, edged `#3f1f7a`, white label), a steal (40% or more) Unique Gold (`#fff1a8` through `#ffd83a` to `#f2bd12`, edged `#8a6400`, dark brown `#3d2a00` ink, its gauge brown). Those colours mean a deal's size on a Deal Badge and nothing else. The gold is a clear yellow with dark ink and a bright top shine, never the doubt chip's amber with white lettering, so it can't be read as doubt.

rules.name: The Over the Game, See-Through Rule
rules.body: A window laid over the game is see-through: the overlay on the Quest Helper's glass. A window on the desktop (setup) is opaque. Same family, different footing.

rules.name: The Two Inks Rule
rules.body: Text on the see-through glass is the Quest Helper's near-black Panel Ink; text on lavender is navy Ink. Never mix them in one window. The panel sets its own `color`: inheriting the body's would carry navy into every figure that doesn't name its ink.

rules.name: The Right-Aligned Figures Rule
rules.body: Numeric columns are right-aligned so EXP, HP, rates and share line up at their ends from one glance to the next. Maplestory's figures are proportional and it has no tabular ones; the body still asks for `tabular-nums`, which the Arial fallback honours.

rules.name: The Outlined Lettering Rule
rules.body: Only a map's title, the Street Name and the Map Name, uses the Mini Map's light lettering outlined in blue (the shared `--title-lettering` text-shadow: a 1px title-outline stroke in eight directions plus one soft 0 2px 1px drop). It appears on the overlay's title panel and in the map setup found, nowhere else. Everything else, Time to Level included, is ink.

rules.name: The Notes Wrap, Names Truncate Rule
rules.body: Notes and the Map Name wrap so they can be read in full; notes, key hints and the arrival's trip wrap with `text-wrap: pretty`, the Map Name with `balance`. Single-line facts (destinations, mob names, route stops, suggestion names, result maps) truncate with an ellipsis instead of growing the panel.

rules.name: The Chrome, Not Lift Rule
rules.body: Depth is drawn the way the game draws it, with highlights, bevels and hairlines. Nothing floats on a blurred drop shadow.

rules.name: The Light Edge Rule
rules.body: Text on the see-through glass keeps a faint light edge so a busy, saturated scene behind it can't swallow it. It is a legibility edge, as the Quest Helper's text has, not a glow: never coloured, never on the bars.

rules.name: The Motion Answers Rule
rules.body: A window moves only to show the player where something they reached for comes from. What the game changes, changes in place.

dos: **Do** build new overlay states from the game's window materials: the grey window bar, the Mini Map's sky-blue title panel, the Quest Helper's see-through glass with near-black text, and the game's bright blue buttons.
**Do** keep setup on its opaque lavender with navy ink and steel buttons under the same grey window bar.
**Do** use a see-through body for windows over the game and an opaque one for windows on the desktop.
**Do** reserve game orange for doubt and problems, and pair it with words and a shape (chip, dot, bordered note) so the state never relies on colour alone.

**Do** draw icons as minimap glyphs (portal ring, mob dot, you dot and the you yellow star) and the Map Preview's rings and arrows in CSS or inline SVG (on a canvas in the Mark Card's close-up), or as 2-stroke line icons on the game's small buttons; the pixel-art owl is the only raster and marks the window (on the site, the logo heads the hero too).
**Do** let notes and the Map Name wrap, and truncate single-line facts with an ellipsis.
**Do** keep the Street Name above the Map Name wherever a map is shown as the overlay shows it.
**Do** draw EXP as the game's own EXP gauge, in EXP Lime: the EXP bar's reading, and a best's EXP/h on its lane. Nothing else in that lime.

**Do** give every button, in every window, hover, pressed and a 2px Edit Blue `:focus-visible` ring offset 2px: game blue on the overlay's window bars, light steel in its body, deep steel for setup's step forward and light steel beside it.
**Do** mark a selected row with Selection Periwinkle and its inset edge, and set a list into the body as an inset box.
**Do** set a window read at rest in the browser (the site) in setup's opaque language, framed in Window Edge on Quest Helper Glass over white, with no shadow.
**Do** let what the player reaches for with the pointer show where it comes from, in one exponential ease-out from a first frame already readable, and honour reduced motion.
donts: **Don't** return to the dark dev-tools card with a stats table on top.
**Don't** use orange, or the outlined title lettering, for anything other than their single roles.
**Don't** add small labels or kickers above content beyond the Street Name in the title panel; a label belongs only to the field or figure it names.
**Don't** let a click on the overlay take the keyboard from the game outside the search view, nor one on the Settings window outside a Change and the Deal Margin field.

**Don't** move what the game changes beyond a cross-fade of 150ms or less, and never loop, pulse, overshoot or time a motion. On the site, motion moves only with the scroll, or answers a click (a Map Leaderboard's band switch): never on arrival.
**Don't** float any window on a blurred drop shadow; depth is highlights, bevels and hairlines.
**Don't** introduce a second typeface or icon fonts.
